newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts sees flat markets, H1 costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts sees flat markets, H1 costs.

text.p: Biscuit maker Arnotts Ltd said on Thursday it expected currently flat Australia market conditions to continue in the short term.
It also said start-up costs at a new factory would impact on profits in the first half of the 1996/97 year.
Arnotts said the move from its current Homebush factory in Sydney to a new factory at Huntingwood in Sydney would be completed by the early part of 1997.

"While the start-up costs associated with this move are expected to have an adverse impact on profit in the first half of the new financial year, manufacturing cost benefits will become evident in the second half," Arnotts said in releasing its results for the 13 months to July 28, 1996.
Earlier Arnotts reported a 7.7 percent increase in net profit to A$60.9 million for the year to July 28, 1996, and posted a final dividend of 14 cents, down from 17 cents the year earlier.
The result included an abnormal loss of A$13.0 million linked to the factory relocation.
Profit pre-abnormals however fell 22.4 percent to A$69.2 million. Analysts had expected pre-abnormals profits of between A$67.3 million and A$75.7 million.
Arnotts said the result was in line with expectations as it had announced to the market with its half year result.
Arnotts' chief executive Chris Roberts said the retail market continued to be generally weak.

"Consumer resistance to price increases necessitated by significant cost increases in manufacturing inputs (wheat and dairy) have resulted in lower volumes in almost all of the company's major product categories," Roberts said in the results statement.
He said, however, that increased product development and marketing spending was expected to arrest this decline in the short to medium term.
Roberts said the ongoing restructuring programme would reduce future group profits by about A$34.5 million before tax, "of which A$32.7 million will be charged as abnormals in 1996/97."
This programme was expected to "deliver ongoing annualised savings in the region of A$16 million before tax by 1998," he said.
"The restructuring programme will help to improve our cost structure by increasing manufacturing and administration efficiencies and streamlining the sales process," he said.
Campbell Soup Co owns about 70 percent of Arnotts.
"The fairly flat market conditions experienced in Australia in the period under review could be expected to continue into the short term," Arnotts said.

"However the wide range of initiatives currently being implemented across all facets of the business will position the group to achieve growth in the medium term both domestically and internationally," it said.
Arnotts' share price was down two cents at A$8.50 at 2.15 p.m. (0415 GMT).
